subject: Learning Methods
title: Sleep Clears the Hippocampus
description: A quick, practical guide to Sleep Clears the Hippocampus.

hook.text: After a night of sleep, your brain can absorb 40 percent more new information than it could the evening before.

buildup.text: Sleep acts like clearing a whiteboard. Transferring memories to the cortex frees hippocampal space for tomorrow's.

discovery.text: Matthew Walker's research shows that the hippocampus has a capacity limit.

twist.text: This explains why all-nighters backfire. Even if you cram information in, you can't absorb new lecture material.

climax.text: Sleep isn't lost study time. It's preparation for tomorrow's learning. A rested brain has space.

punchline.text: Sleep makes room. A tired brain has no space for new learning.

quiz.question: Why does sleeping improve your ability to learn new material the next day?
options: Sleep increases blood flow to the brain permanently
Memory transfer to cortex frees hippocampal space for new information
Dreams simulate tomorrow's learning in advance
